title: Review the story the chart tells
summary: A chart should answer a clear question without exaggerating. Check title, units, scale and the underlying values before sharing.
introduction: A chart should answer a clear question without exaggerating. Check title, units, scale and the underlying values before sharing. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain review the story the chart tells
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A chart should answer a clear question without exaggerating. Check title, units, scale and the underlying values before sharing.

blocks.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(["Monday", "Tuesday"], [4, 5])
ax.set_ylabel("Books borrowed")
ax.set_title("Fictional library example")
ax.set_ylim(0, 6)
plt.show()
blocks.title: Review the story the chart tells

blocks.text: The title states the data is fictional. The zero-based scale shows a difference of one book.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write one sentence that accurately describes the comparison.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not present practice numbers as collected real-world evidence.
For more detail later, use this [Matplotlib further reading](https://matplotlib.org/stable/users/explain/quick_start.html).
